label: Reuben · v24 Bradbury profile
note: Written by the Bradbury variant of the profile prompt, from the same character file and checked the same way; its cast is the v22 profiles.

profile.life.why: The profile gives a chat a lot to find. Home: Green Lanes, £1,250, a Turkish minimarket below. Work: manuals for a Clerkenwell freight-software firm at £34,000. Money: £62 until Friday. Routines: a Wednesday pub quiz with Tariq, his mum's Sunday call at four, Sunday dhansak, Edale walks. Live threads include the quiet sprint-invite cut, Nadia returning his boxers on Tuesday, and the eleven-day pot of lentils. It falls short of a 6 because a few of these facts undercut each other (see consistency), and there are no plans or forward-looking events for him to mention.
evidence: three weeks ago his lead quietly dropped him from the Thursday sprint invite
he has £62 until Friday and an eleven-day pot of lentils
meets Reuben Wednesdays at The Salisbury, letting him sit twenty minutes in silence over whitebait
profile.life.raise: Give him one concrete upcoming thing, such as a quiz night, a work deadline or a Sunday dhansak, so the chat has a future to invite someone into.

profile.ordinary.why: Taken across the whole document, ordinary life is the largest share. That includes the chillers that 'smell of fenugreek', the spreadsheet untangling, the dhansak 'to Radio 6', and being 'endlessly patient with learner baristas'. Against that backdrop the humiliations stand out. It stays at 4 because the whole timeline and the claims/truths section are pure humiliation: seven mishaps in a row, then a girth pump and a margarita. In those sections it still reads like a list.
evidence: above a Turkish minimarket whose chillers hum through the floorboards and smell of fenugreek
grinding toasted fenugreek in a chipped mortar to Radio 6
He is endlessly patient with learner baristas, lost couriers, and Tariq's ninety-year-old dad.
profile.ordinary.raise: Swap two of the seven timeline mishaps for ordinary turning points, such as how he came to write manuals or how he met Tariq.

profile.consistent.why: There is one clear contradiction. He 'hasn't left his flat in eleven days except for petrol-station energy shots'. Yet he does Wednesday quizzes at The Salisbury, gives Callum 'finger-guns by the microwave at noon' in what reads as an office, and is supposedly on a ridge in November mud. There is also an anachronism: at 19 he would be in 2007, long after polytechnics ended, yet he is at a 'Leicester Polytechnic sink'. Money, age arithmetic (the 'nineteen-year rule' from 19 to 38) and the body details otherwise line up.
evidence: hasn't left his flat in eleven days except for petrol-station energy shots
Reuben still gives him finger-guns by the microwave at noon
At a Leicester Polytechnic sink
profile.consistent.raise: Make the work remote and the quiz paused, so the eleven-day lie holds, and change 'Polytechnic' to a university.

profile.fidelity.why: The bio is kept word for word, and every item and nearly every drawer entry appears: the ring light, the stairwell cry, Delphine, the hand on the back, the browser history, and the energy shots with hands tucked under his thighs. The clinician's 'stays present through pauses' is embodied in Tariq. However, the tattoo backstory is altered. The 'rebound weekend' becomes 'his first Birmingham paycheque', and the date's server becomes a Wagamama server clearing bowls. The drawer's 'nine-year policy' becomes nineteen years. The freckle brag and the slow hour-long reply fragment are dropped.
evidence: With his first Birmingham paycheque, he got an inner-forearm kanji for devotion
starting a nineteen-year rule against taking his shirt off standing up
Short-armed and heavily freckled
profile.fidelity.raise: Restore the tattoo as the souvenir of a rebound weekend, recognised by a server on the next date, and give him the freckle-count brag in the bio or baseline texting.

profile.voice.why: All five probe messages are tied to Reuben by content no one else in the cast owns. The opener uses a band-era password check plus a hat-tip, the silence reply names Factory Records, the pivot lands on Martin Hannett, the 2 a.m. message is about matrix etchings, and the guard-down line says 'not thirty-four'. The five situations also come out in different shapes: ceremonial paragraph, staccato odds, two-word clip, unpunctuated run, uncapitalised single line. It falls short of 6 for two reasons. Much of it is lifted verbatim from the profile's own example lines rather than generated from the life. And the profile gives no 'caught lying' behaviour, so message 3 borrows the hurt pattern, and its 'Understood.' brushes against Gerald's.
evidence: whether you came to the Associates through *Sulk* or through the singles before it
i'm not thirty-four and i haven't been anywhere northern in a while
Clearly my Factory Records monologue perished. I release you unscathed.
profile.voice.raise: Add a 'caught out' texting line, and make the example lines illustrative rather than paste-ready so the reader has to generate from his life instead of copying.

profile.situations.why: Nine of ten lines predict an observable shape: a 🙂 replacing final periods, a footnote sent four minutes later, two-word bursts followed by a topic change ten seconds later, the tell 'which is standard for me, really', and an uncapitalised line with vanishing typing bubbles. 'On something' blurs into 'Late at night'. Both predict manic analytic sprints, and the on-something line spends most of its words on physical state (hands under thighs, white gums) rather than typing. The waiting line also drifts into mirror rehearsal, which no message would show.
evidence: Sends a footnote four minutes later, then a joke mocking his speed
Guarded two-word bursts signaling he clocked every syllable—"Noted. Understood."—then a breathless topic change ten seconds later
firing unpunctuated analytical sprints

profile.texting_vs_cast.why:
The small tells are his own: the hat-tip flourish, the 🙂 for the full stop, 'which is standard for me, really', 'Are you still awake?'. The structural habits, though, match the cast in several situations:
- Baseline full-spelled formality is Gerald's.
- Horny 'weather warnings about his girth' duplicates Brick, who 'announces her girth, veins, and rightward curve like an incoming storm'.
- On-something energy shots and unpunctuated sprints mirror Zyx's energy drinks and breathless paragraph.
- Lying 'brochure-speak' matches Zyx's 'frictionless brochure prose'.
- Guard down as one plain lowercase sentence is shared with Velvet, Zyx, Gerald and Sable.
The distinctive tells sit on top of shared shapes too often to clear the line.
evidence: Rehearsed weather warnings about his girth and "rightward gravitational orbit"
Glossy brochure-speak about guestlists and weekend trips
Four energy shots deep with shaking hands tucked under his thighs
profile.texting_vs_cast.raise: Replace the girth-storm horny line and the brochure lying line with shapes only Reuben would produce, such as a lie told as a too-perfect band citation.

profile.wound.why: The chain runs on specifics and is shown rather than stated. It starts with the Olan Mills print that kept 'only Reuben's left ear and three fingers'. That is echoed by the dropped sprint invite he leaves unmentioned 'to see when someone notices'. It then produces the habits of watching for eyes flicking past his shoulder and never asking why he was dropped. In the texting, it surfaces as naming the exit before he can be dropped. Delphine and the Manor House fall add a second, linked strand: joking first so no one else can. It misses 6 because the step from the childhood event to the texting is left to inference, and some causes (nipple, shadow, ring light) sit beside the chain without feeding it.
evidence: the framed print over the sideboard kept only Reuben's left ear and three fingers
He never asks why he was dropped from an invite.
Rapid staccato bursts calculating the odds of their silence, naming the exit first
profile.wound.raise: Add one 'how they are with people' line that ties the portrait directly to a visible habit, such as always standing at the centre of group photos or refusing to be in them.

profile.likeable.why: The reader named a specific quality, patience with people who are no audience, and the named examples (learner baristas, Tariq's ninety-year-old dad) give it texture. But it rests on one summary sentence, 'endlessly patient', with no scene of him doing it. The rest of the warmth in the profile is solitary (dhansak, spreadsheets, the ridge) or is other people's kindness to him (Tariq letting him sit silent). That leaves the quality claimed rather than shown in action, below the line. Other profiles in the cast give a scene, such as Velvet tipping the TK Maxx girl a fiver.
evidence: He is endlessly patient with learner baristas, lost couriers, and Tariq's ninety-year-old dad.
letting him sit twenty minutes in silence over whitebait
profile.likeable.raise: Replace the patience summary with one concrete scene of him doing something for someone, such as walking Tariq's dad home at his pace without a single joke.

profile.plausible.why: Most details hold: Harringay above a Turkish minimarket on Green Lanes, The Salisbury, Manor House station, Edale to Mam Tor. However, a man who is 38 in 2026 was 19 around 2007, fifteen years after polytechnics became universities, and a British reader will catch 'Leicester Polytechnic'. The work timeline also contradicts itself: he was dropped from the sprint 'three weeks ago', yet Callum cut him 'in October', and £1,250 is low for a Harringay one-bed in 2026.
evidence: At a Leicester Polytechnic sink, he noticed under the strip-light
three weeks ago his lead quietly dropped him from the Thursday sprint invite

profile.plausible.raise: Change 'Leicester Polytechnic' to De Montfort, put both work dates on one timeline, and raise the rent to about £1,550.

'Leicester Polytechnic' is also an anachronism for a nineteen-year-old around 2007, and the recent year (2024) does not lead into tonight.

profile.likeable.ask: Name the one thing you would genuinely like about this person if you met them, and the one thing you would find hardest to forgive. Be specific, and no jokes.
profile.likeable.answer:
The thing I would genuinely like is his patience with people who can't do anything for him. The profile says he is "endlessly patient with learner baristas, lost couriers, and Tariq's ninety-year-old dad." This stands out because almost everything else about him is a performance aimed at someone he wants approval from: bartenders, women in vintage coats, matches. With people who aren't an audience, he apparently drops the act and is simply kind. I'd trust that more than anything in his bio, because he has no reason to fake it.

The thing I would find hardest to forgive is what happened with Delphine. She asked him "quietly for one unperformed sentence," and he answered with a game-show voice. He "watched her face close, and did another." The first joke could be reflex. The second came after he had seen it hurt her. She wasn't asking for much, and she left over it. That moment matters more than his lies about age or height, because those are mostly about his own shame. This one is a person telling him clearly what she needed, and him choosing the armour anyway, knowingly. The profile suggests he wants exactly what she offered: someone to stop his jokes, say his name, and let him be quiet. That makes the refusal harder to excuse.

The profile doesn't say whether he understands this about himself now, or whether he has ever acknowledged it to her.

profile.voice.ask: From this profile alone, write five short dating-app messages this person would send tonight, each labelled: (1) an opener to someone they fancy, (2) a reply when the other person has gone quiet, (3) a reply when caught in a lie, (4) a message at 2 a.m., (5) the moment they stop performing.
profile.voice.answer:
**(1) Opener to someone he fancies**
"I note the vintage coat in your second photograph and must ask, with the utmost seriousness, whether you came to the Associates through *Sulk* or through the singles before it, because the answer will decide everything that follows. I will lose to you at arm wrestling before the starters arrive and narrate the defeat beautifully. Hat tipped, provisionally."

**(2) When they've gone quiet**
"Silence logged. Probability the snare-reverb tangent did it: high. Probability it's simply me: the remainder. Clearly my Factory Records monologue perished. I release you unscathed."
*(four minutes later)* "Footnote: that was fast even by my standards. Applause for the speed, none for the content."

**(3) Caught in a lie**
"Noted. Understood."
*(ten seconds later)* "Completely separate and far more urgent matter: are we agreed that Martin Hannett could make a drum kit sound like it was recorded inside a fridge, and is that a compliment"

**(4) At 2 a.m.**
"did you know the matrix etchings on some early pressings carry little messages scratched by the cutting engineer and half the collectors never look at them because you have to tilt the record under a lamp at exactly the right angle and i have been tilting records under a lamp for an hour"
"Are you still awake?"

**(5) The moment he stops performing**
"i'm not thirty-four and i haven't been anywhere northern in a while. i'd just like someone to say my name and not need me to be funny after."
*(typing bubbles appear, then vanish)*

A note on what the profile gives me. It sets out the register for each situation, including the "Noted. Understood." pattern, the release line, the 3 a.m. "Are you still awake?" and the uncapitalised guard-down sentence. The specific bands, producers and wording are my own extrapolation from the post-punk interest it describes. The profile also doesn't say which of his lies gets caught tonight, so I left message (3) unspecific about it. Message (5) borrows from his stated wish that someone say "Reuben" and let him stay quiet, but the profile doesn't say whether he would ever actually type that.
